# What Ory Network API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is. That run is sixteen characters, so a body is it twice over —
# the shortest body the pattern reads, since the count is a floor. It is spelled
# in lowercase where the case does not matter and in uppercase where the case is
# what a case is about: base62 holds the letters of both, so either spelling is
# a body.

patterns: ory-api-key

# The three prefixes Ory lists under Ory Network API keys: ory_pat_ and
# ory_apikey_, which a project API key carries, and ory_wak_, which a workspace
# API key carries. All three are read with the same body, so the cases below are
# that one shape in the places a key is written.

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       ORY_API_KEY=ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ORY_API_KEY=«ory-api-key»

case:     a key in the bearer authorization header an admin api is called with
in:       Authorization: Bearer ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      Authorization: Bearer «ory-api-key»

case:     a key in json
in:       {"value":"ory_apikey_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}
out:      {"value":"«ory-api-key»"}

case:     a key on a command line
in:       curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef" https://practical-swirles-01234567.projects.oryapis.com/admin/identities
out:      curl -H "Authorization: Bearer «ory-api-key»" https://practical-swirles-01234567.projects.oryapis.com/admin/identities

case:     a workspace key in a configuration environment block
in:       "env": {"ORY_WORKSPACE_API_KEY": "ory_wak_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}
out:      "env": {"ORY_WORKSPACE_API_KEY": "«ory-api-key»"}

# The alphabet the thirty-two characters are written in. It is base62 — the
# letters of both cases and the digits. The two characters base64url adds, the
# hyphen and the underscore, are not admitted, and either of them ends a body.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       ory_pat_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «ory-api-key»

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       ory_pat_0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef
out:      ory_pat_0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       ory_pat_0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef
out:      ory_pat_0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef

case:     a workspace key whose body carries a hyphen
in:       ory_wak_0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef
out:      ory_wak_0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef

case:     the other project key whose body carries an underscore
in:       ory_apikey_0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef
out:      ory_apikey_0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef

# The lengths either side of thirty-two. The count is read as a floor rather
# than exactly, so thirty-one characters are not a key and thirty-three are one
# key to the end of its run rather than a key and a character left over. What
# the floor costs is the middle case — a key cut short of thirty-two keeps every
# random character written in front of the cut, and none of them is redacted.

case:     a body of thirty-two characters is a key
in:       ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «ory-api-key»

case:     a body of thirty-one characters is not
in:       ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:      ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde

case:     an alphabet run longer than the floor is a key to the end of it
in:       ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0
out:      «ory-api-key»

# The prefixes Ory writes on the credentials that are not API keys. They stand
# under headings of their own on the same page and are a different credential
# under a different term of Ory's, so all of them stay in the text.

case:     an oauth2 access token prefix
in:       ory_at_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ory_at_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a session token prefix
in:       ory_st_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ory_st_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a session cookie prefix
in:       ory_session_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ory_session_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# The spelling one line of Ory's CLI guide writes a project key as. The page
# that states the format and the page that issues a key both name ory_pat_ and
# ory_apikey_ and neither names this one, so those two are the project key's
# spellings the scan reads and this one is left alone. It is the closest of
# these to a key the scan does read — the word it carries opens on the byte pat
# opens on — which is why it is written out here beside them.

case:     the spelling the cli guide writes
in:       ory_pt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ory_pt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# A word that opens on a kind but carries one more letter before the closing
# underscore. The loop matches the kind, finds the extra letter rather than the
# separator directly behind it and gives up on the candidate without trying the
# other two kinds, so no key of any kind is found.

case:     a kind word with a letter appended
in:       ory_patx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ory_patx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the workspace kind with a letter appended
in:       ory_waks_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ory_waks_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# The snake_case names ordinary code carries, since English has a shelf of words
# closing on ory. What turns them away is the word naming the kind, which the
# second underscore has to stand directly behind, and the floor, which the next
# segment of such a name ends the run long before.

case:     a name whose next segment merely opens like a kind
in:       repository_pattern = None
out:      repository_pattern = None

case:     a name whose next segment opens like another kind
in:       memory_wakeup_timer = 30
out:      memory_wakeup_timer = 30

case:     a name spelling a whole prefix with segments behind it
in:       inventory_pat_index_by_id
out:      inventory_pat_index_by_id

# What a key may be written against. There is no boundary on either side of the
# prefix, so a key keeps its span whatever word character it abuts — and where
# the run of its alphabet carries on past the floor, what carries it on is
# redacted with the key. A hyphen and an underscore end the run instead.
#
# A snake_case name whose segments spell a whole prefix carries one, so where
# thirty-two unbroken characters of the alphabet stand behind it, everything
# from the ory onward is redacted and only the syllable in front of it stays.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       ORY_API_KEY_ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ORY_API_KEY_«ory-api-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      x«ory-api-key»

case:     a name spelling a whole prefix with a body behind it
in:       memory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      mem«ory-api-key»

case:     a word written against a key
in:       ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefsuffix
out:      «ory-api-key»

case:     a hyphenated word written against a key
in:       ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-suffix
out:      «ory-api-key»-suffix

case:     an underscored word written against a key
in:       ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_suffix
out:      «ory-api-key»_suffix

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.
out:      the key is «ory-api-key».

case:     a key between Japanese
in:       キーはory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefです
out:      キーは«ory-api-key»です

# Two keys written together. The three letters the opening is made of belong to
# the alphabet a body is written in, so a body may close with ory and the
# underscore of the next key stand directly behind it; the second key begins
# three characters before the first one ends, the two spans overlap and are
# redacted as one. Written with nothing at all between them the first body
# reaches three characters into the second opening and stops at the underscore
# behind them, so those two overlap as well. Written with a space between them
# the two are separate values, and both go.

case:     a key beginning inside the key before it
in:       ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «ory-api-key»

case:     two keys of different kinds with nothing between them
in:       ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefory_apikey_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «ory-api-key»

case:     two keys separated by a space
in:       ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef ory_wak_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «ory-api-key» «ory-api-key»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. A prefix carries two
# underscores, which standard base64 writes nowhere, so only a base64url
# encoding can hold one — and where thirty-two base62 characters follow, the run
# from the prefix to the end of them is redacted whether or not Ory issued it.
# Such a run is a key's format exactly and nothing in the text tells the two
# apart, so sparing it would spare a real key written the same way.
#
# The digest is the same over-match taking a value a reader had a use for: an
# MD5 is thirty-two hexadecimal characters, which are base62 and carry nothing
# that ends a run, and a SHA-1 is longer still. What holds the other side of it
# is the floor and the prefix — a digest of twenty-four characters is eight
# short of a body, and a hyphen is no character the prefix carries.

case:     the prefix inside a longer run of base64url
in:       payload=zzzzory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefzzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«ory-api-key»

case:     an md5 behind the prefix in a cache key
in:       key: ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      key: «ory-api-key»

case:     a sha1 behind the prefix
in:       ory_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «ory-api-key»

case:     a digest of twenty-four characters behind the prefix
in:       ory_pat_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      ory_pat_0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     an md5 behind a hyphen rather than the prefix
in:       ory-pat-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ory-pat-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# The prefix written in a case Ory does not issue keys in, the prefix without
# the underscore it closes with, the opening with no word naming a kind behind
# it, and a body of the right length with no prefix at all.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       ORY_PAT_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ORY_PAT_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the prefix without its closing underscore
in:       ory_pat0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ory_pat0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the opening with no word naming a kind
in:       ory_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ory_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a word no key is issued with where the kind stands
in:       ory_key_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      ory_key_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
